简单取放.recommendation: The Planner's initial plans consistently decompose simple pick-and-place into two ordered subtasks (find/take target, then put at destination), matching T1_001. Keep this two-stage decomposition; it is sufficient and avoids over-planning.

Successful episodes show the plan should search open surfaces first (desk, sidetable, dresser, sofa, bed, shelf, countertop) before opening closed containers. In episode_001 the cellphone was found on the bed after several closed drawers were checked; in episode_011 the pan was on the countertop after many cabinets. Prioritize visible surfaces before exhaustive container opening.

Plans should include opening a closed destination container before placing. Episode_023 succeeded by opening cabinet 1 before put; episode_001's dresser was already open (open returned Nothing happens) and put still succeeded. Encode 'open destination if closed, then put' in the plan.

When a put fails with 'Nothing happens' because the actor is not yet at the destination, the plan should route to the destination before retrying. Episode_012 shows put failing at the countertop, then succeeding after go to garbagecan 1. Include a navigate-before-put checkpoint.

Plans should treat repeated 'go to' no-ops (e.g., drawer 4, dresser 1) as evidence the location is unreachable or already visited, and switch to a new unchecked location rather than reissuing. Episodes 007, 017, and 024 show repeated no-op navigations before eventually finding the target elsewhere.

The plan should terminate once the put observation confirms the object is at the destination; successful episodes end immediately after the confirming put with no redundant verification. Do not add extra examine or inventory steps after a confirming placement.

Plans should keep the exact object instance taken and reuse it for the put, and should match the exact named object type. All successful episodes take a specific instance (e.g., book 1, pillow 1, cd 1) and place that same instance; no substitution occurred.

For simple pick-and-place, the plan need not include cleaning, heating, cooling, or intermediate placements; all 24 successful episodes are pure acquire-then-place. Keep the plan minimal and avoid inserting extra stages that add steps and tracking risk.

台灯观察.recommendation: When the desklamp is already visible on a surface, go directly to that furniture and use the numbered lamp; do not detour through unrelated drawers or containers first. Episodes 025 and 038 show long drawer sweeps before finally using the lamp, while 026/028/030/042 succeed by going straight to the lamp surface.

After taking the target, do not re-issue go to the same furniture or bare 'go to desk'; these return Nothing happens (episodes 027, 029, 034, 035, 041). Once at the lamp surface, proceed directly to use desklamp <id>.

If use desklamp returns Nothing happens at the current furniture, the lamp may not be there; move to a surface where a desklamp was actually observed and retry with its instance id. Episodes 029, 031, and 040 recover by relocating to a sidetable/dresser with a visible desklamp.

Do not open drawers/dressers/desks blindly at the start; episodes 033 and 036 fail after only open attempts returning Nothing happens, never locating the target or lamp. Navigate to observable surfaces first and open containers only when a plausible target location is closed.

Placing the target on the desk and then using the lamp does not reliably satisfy the goal; episode 027 put the tissuebox on desk 1 and used the lamp but still failed. Keep the target held and use the numbered lamp, as in successful episodes 026/028/030.

Avoid examine/look on the target or furniture as a substitute for the lamp interaction; episodes 029, 034, and 040 show examine/look yielding no goal progress. Use the numbered use desklamp <id> action once at the lamp surface.

When the target is not on the first surface, broaden systematically across plausible open surfaces (beds, armchairs, coffeetables, shelves) before concluding failure; episodes 037 and 039 succeed after searching several surfaces for the target.

Treat a successful 'You turn on the desklamp <id>' observation as the terminal success signal and stop; do not add redundant use/look steps afterward. Episode 034 continued issuing use/look after turning on the lamp and still failed.

清洗后放置.recommendation: Strengthen the clean-then-place plan so the clean step is only considered done after an explicit success observation; if clean returns 'Nothing happens', do not proceed to placement. In episode_071 the plan moved to put after a failed clean, then repeated identical puts on countertop 1 with no effect. Require a clean-state check before the placement stage and a changed approach (different fixture or object) after a failed clean.

When the named object type is unavailable, do not silently substitute a similar type. Episode_052 planned for a knife but placed a butterknife, and episode_059 planned for a mug but took a cup; both failed. Keep searching for the exact type or explicitly confirm equivalence before taking.

Bound the acquisition search and reassess feasibility instead of opening every cabinet/drawer. Episodes 044, 052, 063, and 070 show long container sweeps; 044 and 063 exhausted the plan without finding the target. Prioritize likely locations by object type, track checked locations, and report blocked after a reasonable set rather than continuing indefinitely.

After a put returns 'Nothing happens', stop repeating the same destination. Episode_071 issued repeated identical puts to countertop 1 and sinkbasin 1 with no effect; episode_059 tried coffeemachine, countertop, cabinet, sinkbasin, and garbagecan without changing conditions. Verify held object and current location, then change destination or report blocked.

Treat invalid or non-openable destinations as unusable rather than retrying open/put. In episode_059, open coffeemachine and puts to coffeemachine returned no effect; in episode_063, open stove and puts to stoveburner returned no effect. Confirm the destination is a valid openable receptacle before the placement stage.

For cloth/towel-like objects, do not loop clean attempts at sinkbasin or bathtubbasin. Episode_049 repeatedly cleaned towel 1 and cloth 2 with no effect across both fixtures. After confirming the object is held and at a sinkbasin, if clean still fails, treat the object as not cleanable and try another candidate or report blocked.

Keep the clean-then-place decomposition but make the destination stage conditional on a confirmed clean state and a valid destination. Successful episodes 043, 045, 046, 047, 048, 050, 051, 053, 054, 055, 056, 057, 058, 060, 061, 062, 064, 065, 066, 067, 068, 069, 070, 072, and 073 all follow acquire-clean-place with an observed clean success; failures occur when clean or destination validity is skipped.

When a planned destination is closed, open it before placing, and if open returns no effect treat it as already open or non-openable and proceed accordingly. Episode_055 opened cabinet 1 with no effect but then successfully put bowl 4 there; episode_043 correctly opened drawer 1 before putting. Avoid reissuing open after a no-effect result.

加热后放置.recommendation: The initial plans repeatedly include a 'take the heated object from the microwave' step even when heating is done while holding the object, causing failed take-from-microwave actions. Plan heating as a state change on the held object and only add a take-from-microwave step if the object was actually placed inside.

Plans should specify the correct heat action form (heat <object> with microwave <id>) rather than generic 'use <object>' or 'use microwave'. Episodes 074, 075, 078, 085, 088, 089, 093, 095, 096 burned many steps on 'use X' returning Nothing happens before eventually succeeding with the proper heat command.

When heat returns Nothing happens, the plan should branch to the documented recovery: ensure the microwave is open, then alternate between holding the object and placing it inside before retrying heat. Episodes 077 and 090 show this recovery succeeding; episodes 074/078/085/088/089 looped on identical failing commands instead.

Plans should not substitute a different object type for the named target. Episode 075 planned for a mug but took cup 2; episode 088 planned for a mug but took cup 1; episode 093 planned for a mug but used cup 3. These substitutions contributed to failures. Search for the exact named type or confirm equivalence before taking.

Search plans should prioritize likely locations by object type and avoid opening every cabinet in sequence. Episodes 079, 080, 083, 091, 093, 096 spent many steps traversing cabinets before finding the target on a diningtable or countertop. Check visible surfaces and high-probability containers first, and track checked locations.

Plans should open the microwave before attempting heat, and should not close it mid-task. Episode 089 closed the microwave after taking the egg out, and episode 074 never opened it before use attempts. Include an explicit open-microwave step before heating and keep it open until heating is confirmed.

Plans should treat heating as an intermediate milestone and continue directly to the final destination after confirmed heat, without extra intermediate placements. Episode 074's plan included a take-from-microwave step that conflicted with holding-based heating; episode 077 succeeded by heating while holding then going straight to the cabinet.

Plans should verify the destination is openable and valid before committing to it. Episodes 087 and 093 targeted coffeemachine and failed; episode 080 targeted cabinet 1 which contained other items. Confirm destination validity and openability during planning, and choose an alternative if the destination rejects placement.

冷却后放置.recommendation: When cooling, the reliable pattern is: acquire the exact target, go to the fridge, open it, then issue an explicit cool action (e.g., 'cool X with fridge 1') while holding the object, and only then proceed to the destination. Do not assume that placing the object in the fridge or finding it there constitutes cooling; require an explicit cooled-state confirmation before moving on.

The initial plan should not include a 'take the cooled object from the fridge' step when cooling is done while holding the object. Successful runs cool while holding and then go directly to the destination; adding a take-from-fridge step is unnecessary and can cause no-op loops.

When a put returns 'Nothing happens', do not repeat the same put or issue go/open on the same target. In episode 099 the agent repeatedly put bowl 2 into closed cabinets and got no-ops; it should have verified it was at an open destination and that the object was still held before retrying, or chosen a different valid destination.

Search for the target should be bounded and prioritized. Episodes 100, 104, 106, 114, and 117 exhausted many cabinets/drawers without finding the object and then failed. After checking high-probability locations (fridge, countertops, dining tables, a few cabinets/drawers), reassess feasibility rather than opening every remaining container.

Do not substitute a similar object type for the named target. Episode 109 planned for a mug but took a cup 1, then failed to place it in the coffeemachine. Search for the exact named type (mug) and only use a confirmed equivalent if the exact type is unavailable and the environment treats it as equivalent.

Before placing, confirm the destination is open and valid. In episode 109 the agent tried put, open, and use on the coffeemachine with no effect; some fixtures reject placement. If put repeatedly fails at a destination, treat it as invalid and report blocked or choose an alternative rather than looping on open/examine/use.

After a successful cool action, proceed directly to the destination and place the object; do not add intermediate placements or redundant verification. Successful episodes (101, 105, 107, 110, 112, 113, 115, 116) all follow acquire -> open fridge -> cool -> go to destination -> put, and stop once placement is confirmed.

When the target is not in the first checked location, continue systematically across plausible surfaces and containers (countertops, dining tables, fridge) rather than declaring blocked early. Episodes 103, 105, 107, 110, 112, 113, and 115 found the target on a later surface after the fridge was empty.

双物品放置.recommendation: The initial plan template '(S1 AND S2 AND S3 AND S4)' with S1=find/take first, S2=put first, S3=find/take second, S4=put second is the correct decomposition and appears in every episode. Keep this ordered two-cycle structure; do not merge the two items into a single search-and-carry phase.

When both instances are visible on the same surface (coffeetable, diningtable, countertop, sofa), the plan should place the first then return to that same location for the second, as in successful episodes. Note this explicitly in the plan so the second search does not wander to unrelated containers.

Episode 123 failed: the plan treated a handtowel as the first 'cloth' and placed it, then found cloth 3 on the dresser. The goal named cloth, and handtowel is a different object type. The plan should specify the exact target object type and not accept a similar-named substitute; if only a handtowel is found, continue searching for the named type.

Episode 132 failed: after taking newspaper 2 from shelf 1, the plan searched sidetable, shelf 1, shelf 2, and sofa before finding newspaper 1, and the episode ended without a confirmed second placement. The plan should track that the first item was already placed and drive directly to the second acquisition and final put, confirming each put from the observation.

Episode 129 shows a put returning 'Nothing happens' (step 25) before the agent re-navigated to sofa and retried successfully. The plan should include a per-put confirmation checkpoint: if the put observation does not confirm placement, navigate to the destination and retry before starting the next cycle.

Closed destinations must be opened before placing. Episodes 125, 128, and 130 show the plan opening drawer 1 / cabinet 1 before the put, and episode 126 shows 'open cabinet 1' returning 'Nothing happens' when it was already open, after which the plan proceeded. Include an open-if-closed step for the destination and treat a no-op open as already-open rather than retrying.

Search plans should prioritize visible open surfaces (countertop, diningtable, coffeetable, sofa, shelf, dresser) before opening many closed cabinets/drawers. Episodes 127 and 134 spent many steps opening cabinet/drawer sequences before returning to a surface that held the second item; a surface-first ordering would shorten the second cycle.

The plan should not attempt to take a second object while still holding the first, and should not re-take an already-placed object. Successful episodes always put the first item before searching for the second; encode this as an explicit precondition (hands empty) before the second acquisition.

简单取放.recommendation: For simple pick-and-place, keep the two-phase acquire-then-place structure: search plausible open surfaces, take the exact instance, then navigate to the destination before putting. This pattern succeeded across nearly all episodes.
When a put returns 'Nothing happens', do not retry the same put in place; navigate to the destination first, then put. Episode 012 recovered exactly this way after an early failed put on garbagecan.
When opening a destination returns 'Nothing happens', treat it as non-openable or already open and proceed directly to put, as in episode 001 with dresser 1. Do not loop on open.

Avoid repeated 'go to' attempts on the same unreachable target (e.g., drawer 4 twice in episode 017, drawer 2 twice in episode 024). After one no-change navigation, switch to another plausible unchecked location rather than retrying identically.

Maintain a checked-location record during search. Episodes 007 and 024 show long container sweeps; after exhausting cabinets/drawers, broaden to open surfaces like countertops, diningtable, sidetable, and toilet, which is where the target was ultimately found.

Use exact observed instance identifiers when taking and placing (e.g., book 4, cd 1, keychain 2). This avoids ambiguity when multiple same-type objects share a surface and keeps the held instance consistent through placement.

After a confirmed put observation, stop issuing further actions; the placement observation is the terminal success condition. Successful episodes consistently end immediately after the confirming put.

Open closed containers before inspecting or placing into them, and prefer open surfaces first when searching. Episode 023 correctly opened cabinet 1 before putting the soapbottle; episode 011 opened closed cabinets before concluding they were empty.

台灯观察.recommendation: When the desklamp is already visible on a surface, go directly to that surface and use the numbered lamp; do not re-search dressers or drawers for a lamp already observed. In episode_025 the lamp was seen on coffeetable 1 at step 1 but the agent searched dressers and drawers before returning.

After taking the target object, do not issue a redundant 'go to' the same location; it returns Nothing happens. In episode_027 the agent took tissuebox 1 from desk 1 then immediately tried 'go to desk 1' (no-op), then wandered to sidetable/drawers/garbagecan before returning. Once holding the object at the lamp surface, proceed directly to use desklamp <id>.

When 'use desklamp 1' returns Nothing happens at a surface, the lamp is not there; stop retrying and search other surfaces. In episode_029 the agent retried use desklamp 1 twice at desk 1 (both no-op) before finding desklamp 1 on sidetable 1. Also avoid bare 'go to desk' and 'examine desk 1' as substitutes.

Do not open drawers/dressers/desks blindly when the lamp or target is likely on an open surface. In episode_033 and episode_036 the agent issued repeated 'open drawer N'/'open dresser 1'/'open desk 1' commands that all returned Nothing happens, exhausting the plan without ever locating the target or lamp. Navigate to open surfaces first and only open confirmed closed containers.

When the target object is already on the same surface as the desklamp, take it and use the lamp without leaving. In episode_027 tissuebox 1 was on desk 1 with desklamp 1, but the agent carried it away and searched other locations before returning; the goal was not confirmed. Prefer staying at the lamp surface once both target and lamp are co-located.

After a failed 'go to desk 1' no-op, do not retry the same or bare 'go to desk'; instead use 'look' to confirm current location and then use the lamp if present. In episode_034 the agent issued 'go to desk 1' and 'go to desk' (both no-op) while already at the desk, then used desklamp successfully. Treat a no-op go-to as evidence you are already there.

Successful pattern to reinforce: locate target on an open surface, take it, navigate to the surface holding the numbered desklamp, and issue 'use desklamp <id>'. Episodes 026, 028, 030, 032, 035, 037, 038, 039, 040, 041, 042 all succeeded with this exact sequence; keep it as the default and avoid detours.

When the first checked surface lacks the target, broaden to other open surfaces (beds, shelves, armchairs, sidetables) before opening containers. In episode_037 the agent found the cellphone on armchair 1 after checking desks, dressers, and beds; in episode_038 it found the alarmclock on shelf 2 after many empty drawers. Track checked locations to avoid revisiting.

清洗后放置.recommendation: When a clean action returns 'Nothing happens', do not retry the same object/fixture combination. In episode_049, cleaning towel 1 at sinkbasin 1 failed repeatedly, and cleaning cloth 2 at bathtubbasin 1 also failed; the agent looped across both. After one failed clean, verify the held object is a cleanable type and switch to a sinkbasin with a different candidate object, or report the object as not cleanable.

Do not substitute a similar object type for the named goal object. In episode_052 the goal was a clean knife, but the agent placed butterknife 1 in drawer 1; in episode_059 the goal was a mug but the agent took cup 1 and then could not place it. Search for the exact named type and only use a confirmed equivalent.

After a put returns 'Nothing happens', stop issuing further put attempts at arbitrary receptacles. In episode_059 the agent tried coffeemachine, countertop 1, countertop 2, cabinet 1, sinkbasin 1, and garbagecan 1 in sequence, all failing, without reassessing whether the held object was the correct target or whether the destination was valid. Re-check the goal object and destination validity before retrying.

When the destination is a stoveburner and put fails, do not assume the object is placeable there. In episode_063 the agent held kettle 1 and tried put on countertop, diningtable, stoveburner 2, and use on stoveburner 1, all returning 'Nothing happens'. If the named destination rejects placement after one or two attempts, reassess whether the object type is valid for that fixture rather than cycling through unrelated surfaces.

When a clean action fails and the object cannot be taken, avoid alternating between the same two locations. In episode_049 the agent repeatedly moved between sinkbasin 1 and bathtubbasin 1, re-cleaning towel 1 and cloth 2 with no state change. After one or two no-change results, broaden to a different cleanable candidate or declare the object unsuitable.

When a destination container's open action returns 'Nothing happens', treat it as already open or non-openable and proceed to put rather than retrying open. Episode_055 shows this working: open cabinet 1 returned 'Nothing happens', the agent checked inventory, then successfully put bowl 4 in cabinet 1. Episode_052 shows the failure mode: open drawer 1 returned 'Nothing happens' twice before the agent placed a wrong object.

Successful clean-then-place runs follow a consistent order: acquire the exact object, go to sinkbasin, clean with a confirming observation, then go to the destination, open if closed, and put. Episodes 043, 045, 046, 047, 048, 050, 051, 053, 054, 056, 057, 058, 060, 061, 062, 064, 065, 066, 067, 069, 070, 073 all confirm this sequence. Preserve this ordering and treat the clean observation as the gate before moving to the destination.

When the target object is not found in the first few likely locations, continue systematically across plausible surfaces and containers rather than declaring failure. Episode_044 failed after checking countertops, shelf, many cabinets, and drawers without finding a kettle; the search was broad but never located the object. Track checked locations and prioritize object-type-appropriate spots (kettles near stoveburners/countertops) before exhausting every cabinet.

加热后放置.recommendation: When heating fails, the agent repeatedly issues 'use <object>' or 'use microwave' with no state change. The successful pattern across episodes is the explicit 'heat <object> with microwave 1' command while holding the object at an open microwave. Prefer that exact form first; treat 'use' as unsupported for heating and stop retrying it.

Several failures loop between put-in-microwave and take-out while alternating 'use' commands, never confirming a heat success. After one failed heat attempt, change the interaction form (use 'heat X with microwave 1') rather than cycling object position; if that also fails once, stop and reassess instead of repeating the put/take cycle.

Episode 085 shows blind appliance substitution: after microwave 'use' failed, the agent tried stoveburners and toaster with 'use potato 1', all no-ops. Do not switch appliances without evidence they support heating; correct the microwave interaction form first.

Episode 081 shows the agent abandoning a found mug after a failed heat, searching for a second mug, and succeeding with 'heat mug 2 with microwave 1'. The recovery that worked was the correct heat command, not object substitution. When heat fails, retry the correct command on the same held object before searching for another instance.

Episode 089 shows the agent closing the microwave and issuing 'use microwave 1' as a workaround, which fails. Closing the microwave is not a valid recovery; keep it open and use the 'heat X with microwave 1' form while holding the object.

Successful episodes (076, 079, 083, 084, 086, 090, 091, 092) all follow the same clean sequence: acquire exact object, go to microwave, open it, 'heat X with microwave 1' while holding, then go to destination and put. Reinforce this as the default path and only enter recovery if the heat observation is not a success message.

Episode 095 shows 'put tomato 1 in/on countertop 1' and 'put tomato 1 in/on microwave 1' returning 'Nothing happens' before the agent was properly positioned or the microwave was open. Verify current location and open state before put; after a no-op put, navigate to the destination and open it rather than retrying the same put.

Episode 082 shows a long failed search (fridge, two dining tables, repeated 'use apple 1' no-ops) before the agent finally found apple 1 on diningtable 1 and heated it correctly. When the first locations are empty, continue systematic search of plausible surfaces and avoid issuing 'use' commands on an unheld or unheated object; only heat after acquisition is confirmed.

冷却后放置.recommendation: When a put action returns 'Nothing happens' repeatedly at a valid open destination, stop retrying and re-check whether the object is actually held and whether the destination accepts placement; if the goal destination is a garbagecan or coffeemachine that rejects placement, treat it as invalid rather than looping. In episode_099 the bowl was held but put failed at multiple open cabinets; in episode_117 put failed at garbagecan and drawer despite holding the potato.

After cooling an object at the fridge, proceed directly to the destination and place it; do not attempt to re-take or re-cool. Successful episodes show the reliable pattern: take object, go to open fridge, cool <obj> with fridge, go to destination, put. Follow this exact sequence.

When the target object is not in the first checked location, continue systematically across plausible surfaces and containers, but track checked locations to avoid revisiting confirmed-empty ones. Episodes 100, 104, 106, 114, and 117 exhausted many cabinets/drawers and still failed, indicating unbounded search without bookkeeping.

Do not substitute a similar object type for the named target. In episode_109 the goal was a mug but the agent took a cup and then failed to place it in the coffeemachine; search for the exact named object type before committing.

When a destination such as coffeemachine rejects put, open, and use, treat it as non-openable/non-receptacle and stop issuing further interactions there. Episode_109 shows put, open, use, examine, and look all returning no effect at the coffeemachine.

Before placing, confirm the destination is open or openable; if open returns 'Nothing happens' because it is already open or non-openable, proceed to put rather than retrying open. Episode_099 shows repeated open/put failures at cabinets, and episode_117 shows open on garbagecan returning nothing.

After a successful cool action, verify the object is still held and go directly to the destination; do not issue a take-from-fridge afterward. Successful episodes confirm cooling while holding the object at an open fridge, then place it without intermediate steps.

When a go-to action returns 'Nothing happens' for a location, do not repeat the identical command; switch to another reachable candidate. Episodes 100, 104, 106, and 114 show repeated failed go-to attempts at cabinets/stoveburners that wasted steps.

双物品放置.recommendation: When a two-item goal names a specific object type, do not substitute a different type (e.g., handtowel for cloth). In episode_123 the goal was two cloth, but the agent took handtowel 1 and cloth 3; the episode ended plan_completed_without_environment_win, suggesting the handtowel did not count. Search for the exact named type and only use a confirmed equivalent.

After a put returns 'Nothing happens', verify current location before retrying. In episode_129 the agent attempted put creditcard 1 on sofa while at tvstand (no-op), then correctly navigated to sofa and the put succeeded. Treat a failed put as a location/state problem, not a reason to repeat.

Do not attempt to take a second object while already holding one; the take returns 'Nothing happens'. In episode_129 the agent tried take creditcard 2 while holding creditcard 1, failed, then released the held card before continuing. Place the held item at the destination first, then take the next.

When both target instances are visible on the same surface, take one, place it at the destination, then return to that same surface for the second. Episodes 119, 122, 124, 127, 130, and 134 all succeeded with this two-cycle pattern; avoid searching unrelated containers when the second instance is already visible.

Open a closed destination before placing, and if open returns 'Nothing happens' treat it as already open/non-openable and proceed to put. In episode_126 open cabinet 1 returned no effect but the subsequent put succeeded; in episode_128 opening cabinet 1 first enabled placement. Do not loop on open.

Use exact receptacle identifiers; a bare name like 'countertop' returns 'Nothing happens'. In episode_125 the agent tried 'go to countertop' twice with no effect, then succeeded with 'go to countertop 1'. Refer to the exact numbered identifier from observations.

Track checked locations and avoid revisiting confirmed-empty surfaces. In episode_118 the agent returned to countertop 1 (already empty) and repeatedly attempted unreachable cabinet 4; in episode_121 it re-checked shelves before finding soapbottle 1 on the toilet. Maintain a checked-location list and move to unchecked plausible locations.

Confirm each placement from the observation before starting the next search cycle, and do not declare completion on an attempted action alone. In episode_132 the agent took newspaper 1 while already holding newspaper 2 and the episode ended plan_failed; verify the first put succeeded and hands are empty before taking the second item.

skill.title: 台灯观察：定位目标物与台灯并在台灯所在家具处使用台灯
skill.principle: 先确认目标物和台灯位置；台灯通常固定在家具表面。若台灯已在桌面、边桌、梳妆台等表面被观察到，直接前往该家具，不要继续搜索无关容器或盲目开抽屉。目标物不在台灯处时，先取得并携带目标物到该家具；目标物已在台灯处时，可直接尝试使用台灯，若交互未被接受再确保目标物在手中并重试。到达后使用带实例编号的 use desklamp <id> 触发观察；不要用裸名或复合语法，也不要把台灯当作可携带物或导航点。成功开启台灯即为终止条件，不要在其后追加 use/look。
skill.when_to_apply: 当任务要求 examine/look at 某物 with/under the desklamp，且环境中存在可交互的 desklamp 时。

skill.title: 台灯观察搜索策略：优先开放表面并系统检查容器
skill.principle: 搜索目标物或台灯时，优先检查与台灯相关的开放表面，如 desk、sidetable、床头柜、床、扶手椅、咖啡桌、架子等；一旦观察到台灯，应直接前往其所在家具并在需要时使用台灯，不要继续遍历大量抽屉。若合理开放表面没有目标物，再按容器类型（drawer/cabinet）系统搜索，找到后返回台灯处。避免反复 look/examine 同一位置；没有新信息时转向其他家具或容器。'under the desklamp' 不保证目标物或台灯一定在假定位置，因此假定位置不可见时应搜索其他表面和容器。
skill.when_to_apply: 在台灯观察任务中寻找目标物或台灯，或已到达假定台灯位置但目标物或台灯不在该处、连续观察无新信息时。

skill.title: Microwave heating with observation-driven holding/placement recovery
skill.principle: Open the microwave before taking from or using it, and keep it open until heating is confirmed. Use the explicit heat action form heat <object> with microwave <id> rather than generic use <object> or use microwave. Observations conflict on the required heating state: some successful runs heated the object while holding it, while others succeeded by placing the object in an open microwave and then heating. Treat the holding/placement requirement as observation-dependent. If heating while holding returns 'Nothing happens', place the object in the open microwave and retry. If heating with the object inside returns 'Nothing happens', take it out, ensure the microwave is open, and retry while holding it. Do not repeat an identical failing heat command without changing the object’s position or holding state.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target object must be heated with a microwave, especially if the first heat attempt fails or the object is inside the microwave.

skill.title: Systematic search and continue after misses
